title: Traffic contracts and degradation budgets for autoscaler interoperability
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need a mechanism to declaratively express per-traffic "contracts" (expected latency tail, token budget, and criticality) and attach a degradable budget to each contract so autoscaler and ingress can coordinate graceful degradation during constrained capacity and multi-region failover.
background: Recent incidents show autoscaler handoffs + abrupt regional failovers lead to QoS regressions for high-priority routes. Current probe-only gating doesn't differentiate request criticality or budget for graceful shedding. This ticket designs a cross-layer contract and degradation budget that informs the autoscaler, ingress rate-limiter, and circuit breaker layers.
goals: Define a compact Traffic Contract spec (latency p95/p99 targets, token/compute budget, criticality tier)
Implement in ingress so each request carries contract metadata to runtime
Expose budgets to autoscaler for soft-derating decisions and to circuit breakers for token-weighted shedding
Create simulation harness to validate SLO alignment during failover and heavy load
acceptance_criteria: Traffic contract YAML spec documented in Confluence
Ingress annotates requests with contract blob and sampling telemetry
Autoscaler returns soft-derate signals honoring degradation budget in >95% simulated scenarios
Playbook for multi-region cutover validated in chaos runbook
implementation_notes: Contract modeled as: {tier:critical|standard|best-effort, latency_target_ms:{p95,p99}, token_budget_per_min, degradation_weight}
Ingress adds X-Redwood-Contract header (base64 JSON) for internal routes
Autoscaler implements a budget-aware derate API: /v1/derate?route=... returning proportion to shed
Circuit breaker uses token-based priority queue; when evicting, evict best-effort proportionally more than critical
Telemetry: add contract.dimensions to traces and metrics; expose contract burn-rate metric to Console
design_decisions: Opted for header-carrying contracts to avoid global config churn during rollouts
Degradation budget is a rolling window (60s) rather than absolute tokens to smooth transient spikes
Soft-derate preferred over hard-blocking to allow progressive warmup during failover
risks: Mis-tagged contracts could cause unexpected shedding — plan: safe default to 'standard' and audit logs
Additional header size overhead — mitigated by compact encoding and sampling in egress to external providers
testing_plan: Cluster simulation with traffic mix (critical:30%, standard:50%, best-effort:20%) across two regions with induced regional out-of-service
Chaos test: sequentially kill region A then B and evaluate SLO retention and degradation budget burn-down
Load test with token-heavy requests to validate circuit breaker eviction ordering
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated in ingress Canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% across non-critical routes
Enable autoscaler derate in staging and run two controlled failovers
Monitor contract burn-rates and SLO dashboards for 48 hours before broad enabling
comments: Initial spec brainstorm: prefer compact encoding to reduce header bloat.
Discussion with PM: map product-critical routes to 'critical' tier and add onboarding checklist for customers to opt-in for custom contracts.
updates: 2026-02-25: Drafted initial spec and circulated to runtime/ingress teams for feedback (Aisha).

2026-03-08: Simulation run (staging) showed 87% SLO retention under double-region failover; tuning needed to reduce best-effort shedding impact. Adjusted degradation_weight mapping.
